Phase 8 (OBSERVED): a green unit suite is not evidence. Deleting the one line that makes a repeated live-region announcement audible left 9 of the announcer's 11 tests passing. Only 2 caught it - tools/verify-mutation.mjs now pairs each plausible defect with the test that must catch it.

Phase 8 (OBSERVED): @angular/build:unit-test REFUSES a @nx/angular:package build target - every TEKAD library. @nx/angular:unit-test works and delegates to the same executeUnitTestBuilder after patchBuilderContext, so ADR-011's Vitest decision stands and only the executor name changes.

Phase 8 (OBSERVED): the unit-test DOM is jsdom with NO showPopover, dialog.showModal, inert, element.animate, getAnimations or matchMedia. TransitionEvent is present. The overlay lifecycle proof therefore CANNOT move into the unit runner as 12-overlay-foundation.md promised.

Phase 9 (OBSERVED): emulated encapsulation costs +87.7% RAW SSR HTML and NOTHING compressed - gzip is 4.8% SMALLER with it than without, because the scoping attribute is the same 27 bytes 9,005 times and lengthens the unit the compressor back-references. The cost is the COMPONENT INSTANCE: a component per cell is +51% brotli and 2.8x the elements. ADR-014 inherits it - a table cell is not a component.

Phase 9 (OBSERVED): a component whose selector decorates an element the consumer wrote must style it with :host. Angular rewrites .tk-button to .tk-button[_ngcontent-...], the attribute stamped on elements INSIDE a template; the host carries _nghost-... instead, so not one rule matched. The unit suite was green and the button was 21px tall in the UA's default grey.

Phase 9 (OBSERVED): projected content carries the scoping attribute of the component that DECLARED it, not of the one it is projected into. The form field's .tk-field-error rule never applied and the error text was not red. Rule: a component styles its own host and its own template, and nothing else.

Phase 9 (OBSERVED): @layer works. ADR-007 decision 1 had been load-bearing since Phase 4 with nothing checking it. Measured in Chromium against the built package: the order statement survives, component rules land inside tekad.components, and an unlayered consumer rule beats them with no !important.

Phase 9 (OBSERVED): showModal() supplies the focus trap, background inertness, aria-modal, Escape and focus restoration. Tab across 12 presses never reaches an interactive element outside the dialog; Shift+Tab across 6 does not either. ADR-010's bespoke focus trap is not built - for the MODAL path. The position:fixed fallback remains unmeasured.

phase3.roadmapInstruction: Small. Resist building a state framework.
whyNothingWasBuilt: Angular already ships the adapters: toSignal/toObservable in @angular/core/rxjs-interop ARE the boundary conversions ADR-003 describes. Wrapping them adds a TEKAD name, version and migration cost on top of an API Angular maintains.
No caller exists. A "value | Signal | Observable" normaliser is plausible but the first real component will define its shape better than speculation (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
Signals already ARE the state framework. The useful work is enforcement, which is a review problem rather than a library problem.
phase3.whatWasBuilt: ADR-002/ADR-003 review blockers as no-restricted-syntax rules scoped to packages/**
rules: BehaviorSubject/ReplaySubject banned (state by construction); a plain Subject modelling an event stream is ALLOWED - exactly the line ADR-003 draws
.set()/.update() inside effect() banned; effect() touching the DOM or moving focus is ALLOWED
subscribe-then-set by hand banned; toSignal at the boundary is ALLOWED
NgModule decorator banned in packages (ADR-004, moved here from the repo-wide block - it is a rule about what TEKAD ships)
phase3.selfTest: tools/verify-reactive-rules.test.mjs - 9 cases: 5 violations that must be reported, 4 allowed forms that must not be. The allowed cases carry equal weight: a rule that fires on correct code gets disabled.

checksBothRoutes: a class providing NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR without ever naming ControlValueAccessor - invisible to any rule reading only heritage clauses
gate.legalFixture: a signal-forms control AND a separate CVA adapter in one package - the sanctioned shape; a rule rejecting it would make @tekad/forms/compat impossible to write

smallerCorrections: FormValueControl and FormCheckboxControl ARE importable from @angular/forms/signals despite not appearing in the visible export block. The wrong conclusion was nearly recorded; compiling an actual import settled it.
`touch` (OutputRef<void>, control -> field) is NOT `touched` (InputSignal<boolean>, field -> control). One letter apart. The probe got it wrong on first build and the compiler caught it.
phase7.notBuilt: @tekad/forms does not exist. The control contract is Angular's, and the one piece of genuine TEKAD code implied - the CVA adapter - is placed by ADR-013 in the Phase 9 slice and needs a control to adapt.
phase9Owes: the CVA adapter, built against real controls
its own tests, SSR and a11y obligations - ADR-013 says it is public API
a tree-shaking scenario proving @tekad/forms/compat does not reach a signal-forms-only consumer
phase7.watchdog: tools/verify-forms-assumptions.mjs re-runs the measurement every build. If a future Angular starts REJECTING the combination it fails, and the correction should be revisited.

phase8.adrHandling: a DATED CORRECTION appended to ADR-011, not a superseding ADR - Vitest is still the runner; two mechanical claims around it were wrong and one consequence was unforeseen
phase8.headline: The suites went green immediately. The phase's real work was establishing that green means something.

runner.whyTheAdrsNameFails: 'The buildTarget is configured to use @nx/angular:package, which is not supported' - that is every library in this repo
runner.howTheWorkingOneWorks: calls patchBuilderContext(builderContext, buildTarget) then delegates to the same executeUnitTestBuilder from @angular/build, so Vitest and the runner semantics ADR-011 chose are unchanged
runner.includeGlobBase: the project SOURCE ROOT, not the project root. Secondary entry points live outside src/, so they need an explicit ../a11y/**/*.spec.ts - ../**/*.spec.ts was MEASURED pulling another package's specs into the build.

unitTestDom.consequence: 12-overlay-foundation.md promised the 33-assertion lifecycle proof would move here 'unchanged'. It cannot. jsdom carries the EVENT that ends a deferred close and none of the STATE a deferred close exists to manage; a spec written against a real element here would be a double wearing a real element's name - worse than an honest double, because it would read as browser-backed.
unitTestDom.gate: packages/overlay/src/lib/unit-test-dom.spec.ts asserts each absence, so a jsdom upgrade that lands showPopover FAILS and says the double may be retirable. Same arrangement as ADR-005's assumptions gate.
unitTestDom.divisionPhase9Inherits: logic, ordering, lifecycle and DOM structure in jsdom; top layer, focus, inert, animation, media queries and computed style in a real browser via the Playwright gates

theFinding.what: 9 of the live-announcer's 11 browser tests still pass when its central behaviour is deleted
theFinding.behaviourDeleted: clearing the region before setting it, so the change is observable - without it a repeated message is silently dropped
whichTwoCaught: the one that watches with a MutationObserver and requires the region to have passed through empty
the one that requires the clear to be synchronous while the set is not
theFinding.whyItMatters: 'the text is right' and 'the text was observed to change' are different claims, and only the second is why the code is shaped this way. Nothing in the toolchain knew the difference; 9 tests looked exactly as authoritative as the 2 that mattered.

gatesAddedInPhase8: tools/verify-mutation.mjs + tools/mutants.json + tools/lib/mutation.mjs + mutation.test.mjs - CI gate 18

mutationGate.principle: every gate in tools/ ships a self-test proving it fails when it should. Unit tests had no equivalent and need one MORE - a broken gate fails loudly on its fixture, whereas a unit test that has stopped asserting anything simply stays green.
mutationGate.whyNamedTests: 'the run went red' is not evidence. A mutant that fails to compile fails everything, and a renamed test leaves the run red for a reason nobody chose.
threeRejectedFailureShapes: the mutant SURVIVED - everything passed, so nothing covers the behaviour
the mutant BROKE THE BUILD - zero tests ran, so redness is guaranteed and meaningless
the NAMED TEST IS GONE - something unrelated failed instead, which is the exact decay the gate exists to catch
mutationGate.deliberatelyNot: a mutation-testing framework. No operator library, no generated mutants, no score - those produce hundreds of mostly-equivalent mutants and a percentage nobody acts on. A hand-written manifest of plausible defects clears CLAUDE.md rule 9 on both counts.
mutationGate.safety: the ONLY tool in TEKAD that edits source files. Restores in a finally, on SIGINT/SIGTERM and again on exit, then re-reads each file to confirm; exits non-zero naming the file if it cannot.

discoveryGate.why: the ../** leak failed the build LOUDLY. The same slip in the other direction - a new entry point no glob happens to match - produces a green run of a suite that never executed and says nothing at all.
discoveryGate.method:
asks the executor what it discovered (nx test

--listTests) rather than re-implementing the glob semantics, because modelling the executor's behaviour a second time is how the original mistake was made
discoveryGate.check: an EQUALITY in both directions - discovered must be exactly the spec files on disk under that package
discoveryGate.orphanRule: a package with no behaviour worth testing needs no test target (@tekad/theme is a constant and a type), but spec files with NO test target are a failure - someone wrote those and nothing has ever run them

phase8.exampleOfIntendedShape: packages/button/src/lib/tekad-button.spec.ts does not assert type="button" as an attribute. It puts the button in a <form>, clicks it, and requires the form not to submit - with a companion test proving the environment DOES implement implicit submission, so a passing negative means something.

notBuilt.sizeLimitBudgets: ADR-011 specifies size-limit 13.x with @size-limit/esbuild. Deferred: needs components to measure. TekadButton is a packaging fixture and a budget set against it would baseline something about to be deleted.
notBuilt.axeOnEveryExample: deferred - there are no examples yet
notBuilt.whatDoesExist: the theme CSS budget (Phase 4) and the tree-shaking probe (Phase 2) - the two budgets that could exist without components are gates already

stillUnverified: no screen reader has been run - neither the unit tests nor the browser gates prove a user hears anything; what they prove is that the DOM presents the change a screen reader is specified to act on
Firefox/Gecko, real Safari, mobile virtual keyboards
prefers-reduced-motion in WebKit - and now known to be unreachable in the unit runner too, since jsdom has no matchMedia

phase9.roadmapInstruction: prove the architecture, not fill a catalogue - if any of those hurts here, fix the foundation before adding components
phase9.headline: Four things hurt. All four were foundation problems, all four were found by a gate rather than by review, and none of them could have been found by a unit suite.

precondition.owedBy: ADR-007 Consequences: 'emulated-encapsulation SSR cost must be measured before Phase 9'
precondition.measured: 1,000 x 8 table (~9,000 elements), AOT full mode, renderApplication, three shapes differing in one thing each
precondition.theSurprise: emulated encapsulation adds a quarter of a megabyte of raw HTML and, after gzip, the document is SMALLER than the unencapsulated one
precondition.whereTheCostActuallyIs: the component instance, not the attribute. per-cell differs from emulated by one decision.
precondition.parseCost: MEASURED AND UNVERIFIED - none vs emulated are 2 ms apart against 202 ms of noise; even emulated vs per-cell does not separate. An earlier run appeared to show emulated parsing FASTER; that was noise, and it did not get written down only because the gate prints the spread beside the median.
precondition.decision: ViewEncapsulation.Emulated everywhere, by measurement rather than inertia. None would globalise every TEKAD class name irreversibly for a saving that does not survive compression. ShadowDom stays banned (ARIA IDREFs do not cross a shadow boundary; they resolve to nothing) and is now ENFORCED, which nothing was doing.
precondition.consequenceForADR014: a table cell is not a component

packagesAdded.@tekad/checkbox: FormCheckboxControl - a checked model, no value. Native input, box painted over it, indeterminate as a DOM property.
packagesAdded.@tekad/input: FormValueControl<string> - the other half of Angular's split. Decorates a native <input>.
packagesAdded.@tekad/form-field: label, hint, error - entirely ARIA IDREF wiring, not layout
packagesAdded.@tekad/dialog: native <dialog> + showModal(), driven by @tekad/overlay's deferred close - that primitive's first consumer
packagesAdded.@tekad/core/forms/model-control: the token a control provides so the adapter can reach it
packagesAdded.@tekad/core/forms/field-context: the token a field provides so a control can read its description

theFourThatHurt: A component decorating an element the consumer wrote must style it with :host - a class selector is rewritten to [_ngcontent-...] and the host carries [_nghost-...]. Unit suite green, button 21px tall.
@layer had never been tested despite being load-bearing since Phase 4. It works, and now there is evidence.

A foundation package's spec imported a component; the boundary rule refused it and was right. Split into a stub-driven adapter suite and an integration suite on the component side - better than the version that failed.
Projected content cannot be styled from the component it is projected into. The error text was not red and nothing said so.

formsAdapter.shape: a separate directive reached through TEKAD_MODEL_CONTROL, opt-in via [tkCompat]
whyOptIn: tree-shaking - proved with a positive control
once the directive is on a host the CVA wins and the signal contract on that element is dead; making that implicit would silently switch which form system a control belongs to
formsAdapter.disabledChannels: disabledByForm is separate from the author's disabled input - different owners, and [disabled]=false must not fight control.disable() every change detection. The control reads effectivelyDisabled, the OR.
formsAdapter.touchChannel: the control's OWN touch OutputRef, the same one the signal-forms contract requires. The first version had the adapter REASSIGN a method on the injected control, which breaks the moment two things want to listen.
formsAdapter.theEcho: the hardest three lines. A signal effect is SCHEDULED, not inline, so the obvious `#writing = true` flag is already cleared when the effect runs - it then reports the form's own value back as a user edit and the form goes dirty the moment it is populated. The guard must survive until the effect runs AND be consumed exactly once, or a user edit returning to the form's value silently disappears. Both halves have a mutant.
formsAdapter.teardownBug: Angular calls registerOnTouched again during teardown, when the view is destroyed - subscribing or calling DestroyRef.onDestroy there throws NG0911. Found by the directive's own spec, in the cleanup phase rather than in an assertion.

dialogAndADR010.question: ADR-010 anticipated a bespoke focus trap; Phase 6 narrowed it on reading and said it needed confirming against a real fallback
dialogAndADR010.decision: TEKAD writes NO focus trap for the modal path
dialogAndADR010.theSelfCorrection: the first version of the check asserted focus never LEAVES the dialog and failed. Chromium's cycle is periodic with period 5 and passes through document.body as the wrap point. body is outside the dialog by any DOM test and is also not a control. 'Focus escaped' was false; 'focus stayed inside' was also false. The true claim is that focus never reaches an INTERACTIVE element outside. The assertion was wrong, not the platform.
dialogAndADR010.whatTEKADDoesSupply: the exit animation - an element leaves the top layer the instant close() is called, so a closing transition plays on something no longer on top of anything
dialogAndADR010.stillUnmeasured: the position:fixed fallback path, which is where a bespoke trap may still be needed

gatesAddedInPhase9: tools/verify-ssr-encapsulation.mjs (+ ssr-size.mjs, encapsulation-policy.mjs, ssr-parse-cost.mjs, ssr-size.test.mjs) - CI gate 20
parseCssColor added to tools/lib/color.mjs, so contrast is measured from what the browser PAINTED rather than from the token pair the build computed
phase9.contrastGapFound: verify-contrast.mjs checks declared token PAIRS - on-danger against danger, a filled surface. The field error is `danger` used as TEXT on `surface`, a pair not in the manifest at all. A component reaching for a token in a combination nobody declared is how a build-time contrast gate is bypassed with nobody bypassing it. Now measured from the rendered colour: 9.88:1.
whatTheMutationGateFound: a test too weak to distinguish reading the element from toggling the model - one change event from false lands on true either way
a mutant pointed at the wrong suite - the disable path is edited in the checkbox and caught in the compat integration suite
DEAD CODE - the adapter's first-run guard; removing it broke nothing because setUpControl calls writeValue before any effect flushes. Deleted, with mutants.json recording WHY the mutant went.
a mutant that did not compile - refused, because 'the run went red' is guaranteed for a build break and says nothing about the suite
designChoicesWorthKeeping: no `tone` input on the button - a destructive button sets --tekad-button-background, which reaches colours TEKAD never anticipated without waiting for a release (ADR-006 tier 2)
no [invalid] input on the form field - it had no use rendering a <tk-field-error> did not cover, and a field marked invalid with nothing to say tells a user to fix something without telling them what

errors announced BEFORE hints in aria-describedby, which is not the DOM order - assistive technology reads the list in order, and a user just told their input is wrong needs the reason before the advice
aria-describedby and aria-invalid are ABSENT rather than empty/false - an empty IDREF list is a reference to a missing element
outline, never box-shadow, for focus rings - box-shadow is dropped in forced-colors mode, for exactly the users who most need to see focus
stillOwed: size-limit per-entry budgets (ADR-011) - now measurable, there are real components
an SSR/hydration test per package - the SSR probe measures encapsulation cost, which is not the same as proving these components hydrate
select (needs positioning; Floating UI is now a real decision, 6.4 KB gzip against ADR-010's 10 KB budget)
stillUnverified: no screen reader has been run - what is proved is that the DOM presents what assistive technology is specified to act on
Firefox/Gecko and real Safari - every browser number in this phase is Chromium
parse cost - too noisy to conclude anything

packagingProof2026_09_19.what: Phase 9's two packaging debts closed, plus the entry-point generator owed since Spike B.
gates: tools/verify-consumer-boundary.mjs + tools/verify-consumer-boundary.test.mjs - CI gate 9b. Packs every dist package with the real npm pack, extracts the tarballs into a scratch consumer with no path mappings, and requires: every shipped file reachable through an exports subpath, every public specifier to resolve AND import, every internal specifier refused (src/index.ts, raw fesm2022/*.mjs, a subpath that does not exist), the shipped .d.ts to type-check, no lifecycle script, type:module, sideEffects:false, and every bare import to be a declared dependency or peer.

tools/verify-size-budget.mjs + tools/lib/size-budget.mjs (+ .test.mjs) + tools/size-budget.json - CI gate 14, second instalment. Packed tarball bytes and per-entry raw/gzip 9/brotli 11, 2% tolerance, fails on an unbudgeted entry point, on a package that stopped being measured, and notes a shrink so the committed number can be lowered.

tools/generate-entry-point.mjs + tools/generate-entry-point.test.mjs - writes ng-package.json and src/index.ts, splices the tsconfig.base.json path mapping and the package's test include glob, reproduces all five committed entry points byte-identically, and refuses to overwrite.
packagingProof2026_09_19.instrument: tools/lib/tarball.mjs - a zero-dependency npm pack wrapper plus a narrow ustar reader (GNU long name, pax local and global, checksum verified, unknown entry types throw). The archive's file list is asserted equal to npm's own report: a reader that silently skipped an entry would make every check above it vacuous.
foundAndFixed: @tekad/theme shipped styles/tekad.css and tokens.json inside the tarball and its own exports map refused every import of them - the file the package exists to provide was unreachable. Fixed by declaring the two asset subpaths in the source package.json, which ng-packagr merges into the built manifest. verify-package-format's types rule now applies to script artefacts only, with self-test cases both ways.

packages/core/project.json's test include globs did not cover ../forms/**, so specs for the forms/* entry points would have been discovered-but-unrun. The generator's self-test caught it; the glob convention is now one per top-level directory under the package.
packagingProof2026_09_19.determinism: @tekad/theme packs to 4831 bytes on repeated runs. Compression levels are pinned (gzip 9, brotli 11), because a budget measured at one level and checked at another is not the same budget.
packagingProof2026_09_19.refused: Not size-limit: ADR-011's instrument is corrected in a dated note. size-limit measures a synthetic esbuild bundle - a different artefact, through a dependency, whose number moves when esbuild changes. TEKAD measures the packed tarball with no dependency at all. The hard per-entry budget the ADR was protecting is unchanged.
